Comprehensive Guide to Making Homemade Sourdough Bread
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CONTENTS
1. Introduction
2. Understanding Sourdough
3. Equipment & Ingredient Checklist
4. Creating and Maintaining a Starter
5. The Bread-Making Timeline (Typical 2-Day Schedule)
6. Detailed Step-by-Step Formula
7. Common Variations
8. Troubleshooting & FAQs
9. Food-Safety Notes
10. Resources for Further Learning

────────────────
1. INTRODUCTION
────────────────
Sourdough bread is leavened not with commercial yeast but with a culture of wild yeast and lactic-acid bacteria. The result is bread with richer flavor, better keeping quality, and a chewy, open crumb. This guide walks you from scratch starter through baking, suitable for beginners yet deep enough for advanced hobbyists.

────────────────
2. UNDERSTANDING SOURDOUGH
────────────────
• Wild Yeast: Naturally present on flour and in the air; slower but more flavor-producing than baker’s yeast.
• Lactic-Acid Bacteria (LAB): Produce lactic and acetic acids, giving tang.
• Hydration: Ratio of water to flour by weight. A 100 % hydration starter means equal parts water & flour.
• Autolyse: Resting flour and water before adding salt; improves extensibility.
• Bulk Fermentation: First rise; flavor develops.
• Proofing: Final rise after shaping.

────────────────
3. EQUIPMENT & INGREDIENT CHECKLIST
────────────────
Essential:
□ Digital kitchen scale (1 g accuracy)
□ Mixing bowl (glass or plastic)
□ Dough scraper or flexible bench knife
□ Banneton basket or bowl lined with floured towel
□ Dutch oven, combo cooker, cloche, or baking stone/steel
□ Sharp lame/razor for scoring
□ Oven mitts & parchment paper
□ Thermometer (instant-read helps)

Nice-to-have:
□ Stand mixer
□ Proofing box or warm spot (75–80 °F / 24–27 °C)
□ Spray bottle for water mist

Ingredients:
• Unbleached bread flour (strong white)  
• Whole-grain flour (whole wheat or rye) – boosts fermentation  
• Non-chlorinated water (room temperature)  
• Fine sea or kosher salt  

────────────────
4. CREATING AND MAINTAINING A STARTER
────────────────
Day 1  
• 50 g whole-grain flour + 50 g water (≈26 °C / 78 °F).  
• Mix to thick batter. Cover loosely.

Day 2  
• Possible bubbles. Discard 50 g mixture. Feed with 25 g flour + 25 g water. Mix.

Days 3–6  
• Feed every 24 h (or 12 h once activity increases).  
• Ratio: Discard all but 25 g; add 50 g flour + 50 g water (1:2:2).  

Sign of maturity: Doubles in ≤6 h at room temp and smells pleasantly fruity/yeasty.

Ongoing Maintenance  
• Baking often: Keep starter at room temp; feed 1–2× daily.  
• Infrequent baking: Refrigerate after feeding; refresh weekly.

Levain vs. Starter  
For bread, build a levain (fresh preferment) from starter: e.g., 30 g active starter + 60 g water + 60 g flour. Ferment 4–6 h until doubled; use in dough.

────────────────
5. THE BREAD-MAKING TIMELINE (TYPICAL 2-DAY SCHEDULE)
────────────────
Evening Day 0 – Build Levain (4–6 h)  
Night Day 0 – Autolyse (30 min–2 h)  
Night Day 0 – Mix & Bulk Ferment with folds (3–4 h)  
Late Night – Shape & Cold Proof in fridge (8–16 h)  
Morning Day 1 – Score & Bake (45–50 min)  
Mid-morning – Cool (≥1 h) & Enjoy

────────────────
6. DETAILED STEP-BY-STEP FORMULA
────────────────
Target: 1 large boule (≈820 g)  
Baker’s Percent Formula:
• Bread flour 85 % (425 g)  
• Whole wheat flour 15 % (75 g)  
• Water 75 % (375 g total; 325 g in autolyse + 50 g later)  
• Salt 2 % (10 g)  
• Levain 20 % (100 g, 100 % hydration)

Step-by-Step:

1. Levain Build (4–6 h before mixing)
   30 g active starter  
   50 g bread flour + 20 g whole wheat flour  
   60 g water (26 °C)  
   → Cover; ferment until doubled.

2. Autolyse (0.5–2 h)
   In main bowl: 425 g bread flour + 75 g whole wheat + 325 g water.  
   Mix until no dry bits; cover. No salt or levain yet.

3. Mix & Add-ins
   Add 100 g ripe levain and 10 g salt + remaining 50 g water (hold back a bit if dough feels too slack).  
   Pinch/knead until incorporated (5 min) or use stand mixer 3 min low, 2 min medium-low.

4. Bulk Fermentation (3–4 h at 25 °C)
   • Perform 3–4 sets of stretch & fold every 30 min during first 2 h.  
   • Dough should rise 30–50 % and feel airy.

5. Pre-shape
   Lightly flour bench. Turn out dough; gently round into loose boule. Rest 20 min uncovered.

6. Final Shape
   Tighten surface tension: flip smooth side down, fold edges to center, roll to boule or batard.  
   Place seam-up in floured banneton.

7. Cold Proof (Retardation)
   Bag/cover basket; refrigerate 8–16 h at 4 °C. Slow fermentation improves flavor and convenience.

8. Preheat Oven
   Place Dutch oven inside. Preheat to 500 °F / 260 °C at least 45 min.

9. Score & Bake
   • Invert dough onto parchment. Score ½-inch deep slash (e.g., ‘ear’).  
   • Transfer into hot Dutch oven. Lid on.  
   • Bake 20 min at 500 °F (steam phase).  
   • Remove lid, reduce to 450 °F / 232 °C; bake 25–30 min until deep brown (internal temp ≥96 °C / 205 °F).

10. Cool
   Rest on rack at least 1 h to set crumb before slicing.

────────────────
7. COMMON VARIATIONS
────────────────
• Higher Hydration (80-85 %): Open, custardy crumb; requires stronger folds.  
• 50+ % Whole Grain: Increase water, consider adding prefermented flour.  
• Seeds/Nuts: Add during second fold; pre-toast seeds.  
• Sweet Cranberry-Walnut: Fold in dried fruit & nuts; optional cinnamon swirl.  
• Long Ambient Ferment (no fridge): Reduce levain to 10 % and bulk ferment 8–10 h at 21 °C.

────────────────
8. TROUBLESHOOTING & FAQs
────────────────
Crust too pale → Bake longer uncovered, verify oven temp, add convection last 5 min.  
Dense or gummy crumb → Under-proofed; extend bulk/proof. Also check starter vigor.  
Flat loaf → Over-proofed or shaping tension insufficient.  
Starter won’t rise → Use whole-grain feed, warmer spot (26–28 °C).  
Excess sourness → Shorten cold proof or feed starter more frequently.

────────────────
9. FOOD-SAFETY NOTES
────────────────
• Always use clean utensils to avoid contamination.  
• Discard eye-colored, pink, or foul-smelling starter.  
• Internal bread temperature should reach ≥96 °C to ensure doneness.

────────────────
10. RESOURCES FOR FURTHER LEARNING
────────────────
Books: “Flour Water Salt Yeast” – Ken Forkish; “Tartine Bread” – Chad Robertson; “Bread Science” – Emily Buehler.  
Websites: The Perfect Loaf, King Arthur Baking, The Fresh Loaf forum.  
Apps: BreadCalc, Sourdough Hydration Calculator.  

Happy baking—may your loaves sing (crackle) as they cool!
